summary: Ctrl+wheel and Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus change the global UI size but nothing persists it, so every restart resets it and a user who needs a bigger UI re-sets it every launch. applyUiZoom in js/utils/uiZoom.js reads the factor live from webFrame and never stores it. Fix is small: persist through js/core/storage.js under a key declared in js/core/storageKeys.js, restore early enough to avoid a resize flash, clamp on read, no-op in Browser Mode where webFrame is null.

maturity idea -> planned. diagnosed to applyUiZoom reading webFrame live, with the storage key and restore point named. Board-wide re-stamp against the grown 10-value enum (todo gained research / needs-decision / blocked / deferred on 2026-07-31); every todo card had been sitting on idea or planned because those were the only values that existed when it was written.

Picked up under MPI-450 Gate A. Promoted by 1.4 itself: this release deleted the Ctrl+wheel UI-zoom handler (MPI-432), so Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus is the only UI-size control left - and it resets on every launch, which makes 1.4 strictly worse than 1.3.1 for a user who needs a large UI. Dangling links pruned on the move; checklist.md created.

Built. Key in storageKeys.js, accessors in storage.js, applyUiZoom persists, new restoreUiZoom + normalizeZoomFactor, restore called at js/init.js module top level so the page is never painted at 1.0 and then resized. tests/ui-zoom-persist.test.cjs covers step-persist-restart-reapply (a second module instance via a cache-busting query, because uiZoom captures webFrame at module load), 11 corrupt/out-of-range cases healing to 1.0, and Browser Mode. Negative control run: removing the single persist line fails test 1. Full suite 441 pass 0 fail, eslint clean. Maturity validating - the only open item is the user's own restart in the desktop app.
